faq.q: Who is this a good fit for?
faq.a: Software companies of 30 to 500 people shipping an AI assistant, where several people are prompting their own version and nobody owns the final behavior.

faq.q: Are you a fractional AI product owner or product manager?
faq.a: No. I don't take an ongoing seat on your team. I make the behavior decisions that seat would own, for one AI workflow, in a fixed scope, and hand them to your team in writing.

faq.q: Do you build the agents or the orchestration?
faq.a: No. I design who does what, where work hands off and where a person steps in. Your engineers build and run it.

faq.q: Do you build a full design system?
faq.a: No. I set up the small set of rules, tokens and components your AI tools need to stay consistent, plus the instructions they follow. A full design system is a separate project.
Me, Zvonimir Perkovic. A senior product designer with a frontend background, based in Cleveland, Ohio.

faq.q: What happens after the intro call?
faq.a: If there's a fit, I send a one-page scope and a start date. Most teams start with the $1,500 audit.

faq.q: Why not hire a full-time designer?
faq.a: You might later. A fixed Blueprint tests the agent's behavior now, before you commit to a hire or months of engineering.

faq.q: How much of your time do I get?
faq.a: Each engagement has a fixed scope and price. I take on up to five Blueprint clients a year, so each one gets focus.

faq.q: What do I get at the end?
faq.a: An autonomy contract, a behavior spec, a 12-scenario eval report and a coded prototype, plus a go or no-go call.
Figma for design, and React with Tailwind for coded prototypes.
The Blueprint runs six weeks. On retainer, I work one request at a time with a written update every week.

faq.q: What if the result isn't right?
faq.a: Every deliverable gets one round of written feedback from your team, and I revise it within the week. If the signed-off flow or spec still misses something we agreed on, I fix it before the readout at no extra cost.
No. It's a working prototype for testing and decisions. Building the production agent stays with your engineers.

If you cancel before kickoff, you get a full refund. The audit is billed once the review starts. The Blueprint is billed in two parts, at kickoff and at week 3, and work already delivered is not refunded. If I miss an agreed deliverable, I fix it at no extra cost.

faq.q: Do you need access to our agent?
faq.a: Yes. Evals run best against a staging version. With only recorded conversations, untestable cases are marked as not tested.
Building the production agent, training models, and safety certification. One agent workflow per Blueprint.

weeks.t: Map the handoffs, then draw one flow
weeks.d: First, an agent workflow and handoff map: which agent or person does each step, where work passes between them, where a person steps in, and what happens when something fails. Then one user flow built on that map, which every stakeholder reviews and signs off. This is design work; your engineers own the runtime and orchestration.
A 12-scenario eval against your real agent, plus a coded prototype of the trust moments.
Pass/fail report, a release bar and a clear go or no-go, in one Loom and one 60 minute call.
